findings.description: The WARN-silence test covers budget, skipped_cap and aborted but not the fourth non-failed outcome the SDD names (deadline), and nothing in the file pins the implementer's new classification from judgment call 9 (an empty-content `text` answer with additions > 0 is `error` and WARNs). The deadline case already has an injected-clock harness at line 138, so the gap is cheap to close.
findings.failure_mode: A regression that writes the WARN for deadline files would pass this suite and emit one stderr line per remaining listed file on a large PR after the 120 s cutoff; conversely the empty-content → error+WARN path can silently change or disappear without any test turning red.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `deadline` sub-case to the silence test using the `{ now }` clock seam (reuse the times array from line 141) and assert `warns` is empty for the deadline-tagged files; add an outcome row `["empty text", { kind: "text", content: "", bytes: 0 }, "error"]` to the WARN matrix at line 327 so the judgment-call-9 behaviour is pinned.
findings.failure_scenario: A regression that writes the WARN for deadline files would pass this suite and emit one stderr line per remaining listed file on a large PR after the 120 s cutoff; conversely the empty-content → error+WARN path can silently change or disappear without any test turning red.

findings.description: `captured` swaps the process-global `process.stderr.write` for the duration of the awaited call and the replacement discards the `encoding`/`callback` parameters. This is safe under node:test's default sequential execution, but the enclosing `describe` does not pin `{ concurrency: 1 }`, and any future write-site that awaits the write callback (e.g. `await new Promise(r => process.stderr.write(line, r))`) would hang the test instead of failing.
findings.failure_mode: If the suite is ever run with a concurrency option or another test in the same process writes to stderr while a `captured` call is in flight, captured lines leak between tests and the exact-array assertions at lines 336 and 360 become order-dependent flakes; a callback-style writer hangs the test until the runner timeout.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass `{ concurrency: 1 }` to the `describe` at line 311, and make the replacement forward a trailing function argument: `(c: unknown, ...rest: unknown[]) => { err += String(c); const cb = rest.find((a) => typeof a === "function"); if (cb) (cb as () => void)(); return true; }`.
findings.failure_scenario: If the suite is ever run with a concurrency option or another test in the same process writes to stderr while a `captured` call is in flight, captured lines leak between tests and the exact-array assertions at lines 336 and 360 become order-dependent flakes; a callback-style writer hangs the test until the runner timeout.

findings.description: sdd.md § 4 publishes the line as `[bridgebuilder] WARN: content read of <file> failed: <outcome> (no_patch)`; the test pins a JSON-quoted operand (`content read of "src/new.ts" failed`). Implementer judgment call 7 / DEC-1098 chose the quoting deliberately, but the design text and `resources/exclusions-and-coverage.md` were not shown to be updated to the quoted form, so the documented UI contract and the pinned behaviour disagree.
findings.failure_mode: Anyone matching the stderr line against the SDD literal (log scrapers, the G-3 live probe, future tests written from the design) gets a mismatch on the filename boundary; the discrepancy is documented only in a decision row, not in the contract the operators read.
findings.suggested_fix: Update sdd.md § 4 and `resources/exclusions-and-coverage.md` to show the quoted, bounded operand (`content read of "<file>" failed: <outcome> (no_patch)`) with a one-line pointer to DEC-1098, or drop the quoting in `boundedForLog` for this line if the SDD literal is the intended contract.
findings.failure_scenario: Anyone matching the stderr line against the SDD literal (log scrapers, the G-3 live probe, future tests written from the design) gets a mismatch on the filename boundary; the discrepancy is documented only in a decision row, not in the contract the operators read.
